newsitem.title: USA: Singer Brown settles assault case out of court.
newsitem.headline: Singer Brown settles assault case out of court.

text.p: Singer Bobby Brown avoided a court appearance and possible jail sentence, at least temporarily, after charges that he savagely beat a man while vacationing at Disney World were dropped on Thursday.

Charges against Brown and two co-defendants were dropped after the victim, Neil Kelly, 38, reached an out-of-court settlement on Wednesday for an undisclosed amount, Brown's lawyer Robert Buonauro said.

Brown, 27, who is married to pop diva Whitney Houston, has a history of run-ins with the law dating back to his youth in Boston. He faced a felony charge of aggravated battery and could have been sentenced to three years in prison if convicted.
The trial was due to begin on Thursday but prosecutors arrived without Kelly, their star witness.
The judge refused to grant prosecutors additional time to subpoena the Chicago medical technician so prosecutor Bob Welch decided against going forward with his case.
"We can refile and we may well do that," he said. "That's a very, very strong possibility. We feel it's just appropriate to go ahead and resolve it through the court system."

Kelly initially demanded $6.6 million, which he later dropped to $2.5 million. Although Buonauro would not give a figure he said Brown had agreed to settle rather than pay "several hundred thousand dollars" in legal fees.
"This thing has been about money from day one. Three or four people were minding their own business, then Mr. Kelly entered the scene," the lawyer said outside the courthouse.
Asked if Brown was relieved, he said: "At this point he is but he still has that cloud hanging over this."
Police say Brown was socializing with friends at the Mannequin Dance Palace at Disney World in April 1995 when Kelly aproached a woman in the group.
Witnesses say Brown's bodyguard Gary Smith, 29, knocked Kelly to the floor with a single punch. Buonauro said Brown never touched Kelly and Smith was protecting the singer.
But police said Brown and his publicist Travis Boyce, 27, joined in kicking Kelly repeatedly even after he lost consciousness. Boyce contends he was just a bystander.

Kelly's ear was partially severed and was reattached at a hospital. Dozens of fans showed up at the court house, most of them hoping to see Houston, who was expected to attend. But Houston and Brown never came to Orlando.
